› Ethernet Services

AUTOSAR Classic Ethernet Services

Das Ethernet-Cluster realisiert IP-basierte Fahrzeugvernetzung, BroadR-Reach/100BASE-T1 Kommunikation, TCP/UDP-Stacks, IPv4/IPv6-Adressierung und Service-orientierte Schnittstellen.

DoIP

DoIP_ActivationLineSwitch function

This function is to be used by integrators to inform the DoIP implementation about the status of the activation line of a DoIP interface with given InterfaceId.

void DoIP_ActivationLineSwitch(uint8 InterfaceId, boolean* Active);
DoIP_AllowNonTlsDoIPConnection function

Call with argument NonTlsAllowed==TRUE to allow unsecured DoIP connection establishments. If called with NonTlsAllowed==FALSE, DoIP will close the unsecured connection with NRC 0x07 and require the tester to use TLS.

void DoIP_AllowNonTlsDoIPConnection(boolean NonTlsAllowed);
DoIP_GetVersionInfo function

Returns the version information of this module.

void DoIP_GetVersionInfo(Std_VersionInfoType* versioninfo);
DoIP_IfCancelTransmit function

Requests cancellation of an ongoing transmission of a PDU in a lower layer communication module.

Std_ReturnType DoIP_IfCancelTransmit(PduIdType TxPduId);
DoIP_IfTransmit function

Requests transmission of a PDU.

Std_ReturnType DoIP_IfTransmit(PduIdType TxPduId, const PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);
DoIP_Init function

This service initializes all global variables of the DoIP module. After return of this service the Do IP module is operational.

void DoIP_Init(const DoIP_ConfigType* DoIPConfigPtr);
DoIP_LocalIpAddrAssignmentChg function

This function gets called by the SoAd if an IP address assignment related to a socket connection changes (i.e. new address assigned or assigned address becomes invalid).

void DoIP_LocalIpAddrAssignmentChg(SoAd_SoConIdType SoConId, TcpIp_IpAddrStateType State);
DoIP_MainFunction function

Schedules the Diagnostic over IP module. (Entry point for scheduling)

void DoIP_MainFunction(void);
DoIP_SoAdIfRxIndication function

Indication of a received PDU from a lower layer communication interface module.

void DoIP_SoAdIfRxIndication(PduIdType RxPduId, const PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);
DoIP_SoAdIfTxConfirmation function

The lower layer communication interface module confirms the transmission of a PDU, or the failure to transmit a PDU.

void DoIP_SoAdIfTxConfirmation(PduIdType TxPduId, Std_ReturnType result);
DoIP_SoAdTpCopyRxData function

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr.

BufReq_ReturnType DoIP_SoAdTpCopyRxData(PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
DoIP_SoAdTpCopyTxData function

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr.

BufReq_ReturnType DoIP_SoAdTpCopyTxData(PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);
DoIP_SoAdTpRxIndication function

Called after an I-PDU has been received via the TP API, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not.

void DoIP_SoAdTpRxIndication(PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
DoIP_SoAdTpStartOfReception function

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0.

Eth_BufIdxType type

Ethernet buffer identifier type.

Eth_ConfigType type

Implementation specific structure of the post build configuration

Eth_CounterType type

Type Eth_CounterType.

Eth_DataType type

This type defines the Ethernet data type used for data transmission. Its definition depends on the used CPU.

Eth_FilterActionType type

The Enumeration Type Eth_ Filter Action Type describes the action to be taklen for the MAC address given in *Phys Addr Ptr.

Eth_FrameType type

This type defines the Ethernet frame type used in the Ethernet frame header

Eth_MacVlanType type

This type is used to read out addresses from the address resolution logic (A RL) table of the switch. typedef struct { uint8 Mac Addr[6U]; uint16 Vlan Id; uint32 Switch Port; } Eth_ Mac Vlan Type; In case of Macaddr contains a Multicast Address Mac Vlan Type.Switch Port shall be handled as Bitmask, each bit represents a Switch Port , Bit 0 represents Eth Swicht Port Idx = 0 , Bit 1 represents Eth Swicht Port Idx = 1 and so on. In case of Macaddr contains not a Multicast Address Mac Vlan Type.Switch Port shall be handled as a value representing the Eth Switch Port Idx.

Eth_ModeType type

This is an generic type and used in the layers of the Ethernet communication stack (e.g. EthIf, Eth, EthSwt, EthTrcv) to enable and disable, resp ectively, the Ethernet communcation channel and set the corresponding hardware (e.g. Ethernet controller, Ethernet Switch port, Ethernet transceiver) to an lowpower sleep and power on mode, respectively. Tags: atp.Status=obsolete

Eth_ModeType#2 type

This is an generic type and used in the layers of the Ethernet commun ication stack (e.g. Eth If, Eth, Eth Swt, Eth Trcv) to enable and disable, respectively, the Ethernet communcation channel and set the corresponding hardware (e.g. Ethernet controller, Ethernet Switch port, Ethernet transceiver) to an lowpower sleep and po wer on mode, respectively. The type also support to transfer a wake - up request from the services layer (Com M) to the communication drivers (Eth Trcv). This could be used e.g. for Ethernet hardware that has the capability to wake - up and sleep on data line (see OA TC10) Tags: atp.Status=draft

Eth_RateRatioType type

Variables of this type are used to express frequency ratios.

Eth_RxStatsType type

Type Eth_RxStatsType.

Eth_RxStatusType type

Used as out parameter in Eth_ Receive() indicates whether a frame has been received and if so, whether more frames are available or frames go t lost.

Eth_StateType type

Status supervision used for Development Error Detection. The state shall be available for debugging.

Eth_TimeIntDiffType type

Variables of this type are used to express time differences.

Eth_TimeStampQualType type

Depending on the HW, quality information regarding the evaluated time stamp might be supported. If not supported, the value shall be always Valid. For Uncertain and Invalid values, the upper layer shall discard the time stamp.

Eth_TimeStampType type

Variables of this type are used for expressing time stamps including relative time and absolute calendar time. The absolute time starts at 1970 - - 01. 0 to 281474976710655s == 3257812230d [0x FFFF FFFF FFFF] 0 to 999999999ns [0x3B9A C9FF] invalid value in nanoseconds: [0x3B9A CA00] to [0x3FFF FFFF] Bit 30 and 31 reserved, default: 0

Eth_TxErrorCounterValuesType type

Type Eth_TxErrorCounterValuesType.

Eth_TxStatsType type

Statistic counter for diag nostics.

EthIf_CheckWakeup function

This API request the affected Ethernet hardware to c heck for a signaled wake - up. The used Ethernet hardware could be an Ethernet switch or Ethernet transceiver (PHY). This is used e.g. for Ethernet hardware which is compliant to the specification of Open Alliance TC10. This API is called by the integration code. The function could be called in context of the interrupt or on task level.

EthSwt_CheckWakeup function

API is called by EthIf. The Ethernet switch driver request to check for a wake-up at all Ethernet switch ports which reference an EthTrcv. For those Ethernet switch ports the call is forwarded to the referenced EthTrcv. The function could be called in context of an interrupt service routine or on task level Note: Interrupt service routine consuming time has to be considered, since all EthSwtPorts of the maintained Ethernet switches has to be checked. Therefore the call is forwarded to the referred EthTrcv where the request to check for wake-up is stored. The check of the Ethernet hardware is done asynchronously in the context of the EthTrcv_MainFunction.

Std_ReturnType EthSwt_CheckWakeup(uint8 SwitchIdx);

Obtains the port over which this MAC-address at the indexed switch can be reached. The result might be used for a DHCP-server which will need the port/MAC-resolution. If for the PortIdxPtr the maximal possible value (255) is returned the given MAC address cannot be reached via a port of this switch. If multiple ports were found the API returns E_NOT_OK.

EthSwt_GetPortMacAddrVlan function

Obtains an Ethernet switch port bit map, where the given MAC-address with respect to the given VLAN-ID is assigned to. The return argument PortBitMapPtr points to uint32 value which shall be handled as Ethernet switch port bit map. Each bit of the Ethernet switch port bit map represents an EthSwtPortIdx, where the least significant bit (bit 0) represents EthSwitchPortIdx 0 and most significant bit (bit 32) represents EthSwitchPortIdx 31 (e.g. 0x0001 == EthSwitch PortIdx 0 is set; 0x8005 == EthSwitchPortIdx 0, 2 and 31 are set).

Std_ReturnType EthSwt_GetPortMacAddrVlan(uint8 SwitchIdx, const uint8* MacAddrPtr, const uint16* VlanIdPtr, uint32* PortBitMapPtr);

EthSwt_PortEnableTimeStamp function

Activates egress time stamping on a dedicated message object on a dedicated port of a Switch if EthSwtPortTimeStampSupport is set to TRUE for this port. The selective activation of dedicated message objects for time stamping reduces the number of notification calls only to the required calls. Some HW does store once the egress time stamp marker and some HW needs it always before transmission. There will be no disabled functionality, due to the fact, that the message type is always "time stamped" by network design.

Std_ReturnType EthSwt_PortEnableTimeStamp(uint8 CtrlIdx, Eth_BufIdxType BufIdx, EthSwt_MgmtInfoType* MgmtInfoPtr);

EthSwt_ConfigType type

Implementation specific structure of the post build configuration.

EthSwt_MacLearningType type

The interpretation of this value

EthSwt_MgmtInfoType type

Type for holding the management information received/transmitted on Switches (ports).

EthSwt_MgmtObjectType type

Provides information about all struct member elements. The ownership gives information whether EthSwt has finished its activities in providing all struct member elements.

EthSwt_MgmtObjectValidType type

Will be set from EthSwt and marks EthSwt_MgmtObject as valid or not. So the upper layer will be able to detect inconsistencies.

EthSwt_MgmtOwner type

Holds information if upper layer or EthSwt is owner of mgmt_obj.

EthSwt_PortMirrorCfgType type

The EthSwt_PortMirrorCfgType specify the port mirror configuration which is set up per Ethernet switch. The configuration is written to the Ethernet switch driver by calling EthSwt_WritePortMirror Configuration. One port mirror configuration is maintained per Ethernet Switch.

EthSwt_PortMirrorStateType type

Type to request or obtain the port mirroring state (enable/disable) for a particular port mirror configuration per Ethernet switch.

EthSwt_StateType type

Status supervision used for Development Error Detection. The state shall be available for debugging.

EthTrcv

<EthTrcvWakeUpCallout> function

Indicates an wake-up request for the specified Ethernet Transceiver. The given TrcvMode indicates if the request is based on a remote request from the network (ETH_MODE_ACTIVE) or if the request is based on active user request (ETH_MODE_ACTIVE_WITH_WAKEUP_ REQUEST). The callback function Ccan be used to trigger integrator code that initiates a remote wake-up .(e.g. trigger a wake-up line for an active user request).

void <EthTrcvWakeUpCallout>(uint8 TrcvIdx, Eth_ModeType TrcvMode);

EthTrcv_BaudRateType type

This type defines the Ethernet baud rate. The baud rate gets either negotiated between the connected transceivers or has to be configured.

EthTrcv_CableDiagResultType type

Describes the results of the cable diagnostics.

EthTrcv_ConfigType type

Implementation specific structure of the post build configuration

EthTrcv_DuplexModeType type

This type defines the Ethernet duplex mode. The duplex mode gets either negotiated between the connected transceivers or has to be configured.

EthTrcv_LinkStateType type

This type defines the Ethernet link state. The link state changes after an Ethernet cable gets plugged in and the transceivers on both ends negotiated the transmission parameters (i.e. baud rate and duplex mode)

EthTrcv_MacMethodType type

This type defines the media access control type in half duplex. If ETHTRCV_MAC_TYPE_PLCA is configured, PLCA is supported and the parameters listed in ECUC_EthTrcv_00055 have to be configured. Tags: atp.Status=draft

EthTrcv_PhyLoopbackModeType type

Describes the possible PHY loopback modes

EthTrcv_PhyTestModeType type

Describes the possible PHY test modes

EthTrcv_PhyTxModeType type

Describes the possible PHY transmit modes

EthTrcv_StateType type

Status supervision used for Development Error Detection. The state shall be available for debugging.

EthTrcv_WakeupModeType type

This type controls the transceiver wake up modes and/ or clears the wake - up reason. Tags: atp.Status=obsolete

EthTrcv_WakeupReasonType type

This type defines the transceiver wake up reasons.

SoAd_RxIndication function

The TCP/IP stack calls this primitive after the reception of data on a socket. The socket identifier along with configuration information determines which module is to be called.

void SoAd_RxIndication(TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, const TcpIp_SockAddrType* RemoteAddrPtr, const uint8* BufPtr, uint16 Length);
SoAd_SetRemoteAddr function

By this API service the remote address (IP address and port) of the specified socket connection shall be set.

Std_ReturnType SoAd_SetRemoteAddr(SoAd_SoConIdType SoConId, const TcpIp_SockAddrType* RemoteAddrPtr);
SoAd_SetUniqueRemoteAddr function

This API service shall either return the socket connection index of the SoAdSocketConnection Group where the specified remote address (IP address and port) is set or assign the remote address to an unused socket connection from the same SoAdSocketConnectionGroup.

Std_ReturnType SoAd_SetUniqueRemoteAddr(SoAd_SoConIdType SoConId, const TcpIp_SockAddrType* RemoteAddrPtr, SoAd_SoConIdType* AssignedSoConIdPtr);
SoAd_TcpAccepted function

This service gets called if the stack put a socket into the listen mode before (as server) and a peer connected to it (as client). In detail: The TCP/IP stack calls this function after a socket was set into the listen state with TcpIp_TcpListen() and a TCP connection is requested by the peer.

Std_ReturnType SoAd_TcpAccepted(TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketIdConnected, const TcpIp_SockAddrType* RemoteAddrPtr);
SoAd_TcpConnected function

This service gets called if the stack initiated a TCP connection before (as client) and the peer (the server) acknowledged the connection set up. In detail: The TCP/IP stack calls this function after a socket was requested to connect with TcpIp_TcpConnect() and a TCP connection is confirmed by the peer. The parameter value of SocketId equals the SocketId value of the preceeding TcpIp_TcpConnect() call.

void SoAd_TcpConnected(TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId);

of the event just encountered. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None Description This service gets called if the stack encounters a condition described by the values in Event.

void SoAd_TcpIpEvent(TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, TcpIp_EventType Event);

void SoAd_TxConfirmation(TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, uint16 Length);

Up_[SoAd][If]RxIndication function

Indication of a received PDU from a lower layer communication interface module.

void <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ If ] RxIndication(PduIdType RxPduId, const PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);
Up_[SoAd][If]TriggerTransmit function

Within this API, the upper layer module (called module) shall check whether the available data fits into the buffer size reported by PduInfoPtr->SduLength. If it fits, it shall copy its data into the buffer provided by PduInfoPtr->SduDataPtr and update the length of the actual copied data in PduInfoPtr->SduLength. If not, it returns E_NOT_OK without changing PduInfoPtr.

Std_ReturnType <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ If ] TriggerTransmit(PduIdType TxPduId, PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);
Up_[SoAd][If]TxConfirmation function

The lower layer communication interface module confirms the transmission of a PDU, or the failure to transmit a PDU.

void <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ If ] TxConfirmation(PduIdType TxPduId, Std_ReturnType result);
Up_[SoAd][Tp]CopyRxData function

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr.

BufReq_ReturnType <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ Tp ] CopyRxData(PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Up_[SoAd][Tp]CopyTxData function

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr.

BufReq_ReturnType <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ Tp ] CopyTxData(PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);
Up_[SoAd][Tp]StartOfReception function

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0.

BufReq_ReturnType <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ Tp ] StartOfReception(PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType TpSduLength, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Up_[SoAd][Tp]TpRxIndication function

Called after an I-PDU has been received via the TP API, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not.

void <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ Tp ] TpRxIndication(PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
Up_[SoAd][Tp]TpTxConfirmation function

This function is called after the I-PDU has been transmitted on its network, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not.

void <Up>_ [ SoAd ][ Tp ] TpTxConfirmation(PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);

Provides hardware-independent IP network services, frame abstraction, and driver control for Ethernet communication.
AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: not controllable · Prompt: 0af738a94164 Provenance Open questions (2)
Causal anchor: R20-11 Valid from R20-11 Synthesized for this specification release.

translated from the German guidegemini-3.8-flash-low · 2026-10-13 · German original

Provides hardware-independent IP network services, frame abstraction, and driver control for Ethernet communication.

The Ethernet Services module cluster, with Eth, EthIf, and TcpIp, provides the standardized communication infrastructure for Ethernet networks in AUTOSAR Classic ([SWS_Eth_00077], [SWS_TCPIP_00056]). It handles data transmissions via a two-stage buffering and confirmation procedure and transparently routes incoming frames to upper socket layers via VLAN and IP filters ([SWS_EthIf_00075], [SWS_TCPIP_00169]). Robust operating modes, TC10 wakeup routines, and comprehensive RFC diagnostic counters ensure deterministic vehicle operation ([SWS_EthIf_00034], [SWS_Eth_00226]).

In the AUTOSAR Classic Platform (R20-11), the “Ethernet Services” module cluster provides the complete protocol and abstraction chain for packet-based in-vehicle networks. It comprises the modules Eth (MCAL controller driver), EthIf (hardware-independent interface abstraction and VLAN management), and TcpIp (network and transport layer with IPv4/IPv6, TCP, UDP, and ARP) ([SWS_Eth_00077], [SWS_EthIf_00075], [SWS_TCPIP_00056]). Via standardized interfaces, the cluster integrates upper layers such as the Socket Adaptor (SoAd) for service-oriented communication and DoIP (SWS_TcpIp p. 123).

Context diagram: Layered architecture and system context of the Ethernet Services cluster with module interactions. Sources: SWS_TcpIp p. 123, AUTOSAR_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 87, [SWS_EthIf_00075]

During transmission, the data path relies on a coordinated buffering concept: upper layers request hardware resources synchronously via EthIf_ProvideTxBuffer(), whereupon Eth locks the buffer ([SWS_Eth_00077]). After filling, EthIf_Transmit() triggers the transmission, adds VLAN tags, and passes the data via Eth_Transmit() to the MAC controller ([SWS_Eth_00087], [SWS_EthIf_00075]). Confirmation occurs asynchronously, either via interrupt or cyclically via EthIf_MainFunctionTx() ([SWS_EthIf_00091], [SWS_EthIf_00115]). Incoming frames are received via EthIf_RxIndication() and, after controller and address validation, passed via <Up_RxIndication>() to the responsible socket ([SWS_EthIf_00085], [SWS_TCPIP_00169], [SWS_TCPIP_00223]).

Sequence diagram: Buffer allocation, data transmission, and asynchronous transmit confirmation in the Ethernet cluster. Sources: [SWS_Eth_00077], [SWS_Eth_00087], [SWS_EthIf_00075], [SWS_EthIf_00091]

Lifecycle and network operation are managed via controller states (EthIf_SetControllerMode()) and communication modes (TcpIp_RequestComMode()) ([SWS_EthIf_00034], [SWS_TCPIP_00070]). The cluster supports wakeup validations according to OPEN Alliance TC10 via EthIf_CheckWakeup() ([SWS_EthIf_00244], SWS_ECUStateManager p. 192). For diagnostics and error detection, Eth and EthIf provide standardized RFC error counters, signal quality measurements, and DET runtime checks ([SWS_Eth_00226], [SWS_EthIf_91056], [SWS_Eth_00228]).

System architecture and role of the module cluster

In the AUTOSAR Classic Platform (Release R20-11), the “Ethernet Services” module cluster forms the functional backbone for wired, packet-based communication via Ethernet networks. It spans an end-to-end abstraction arc from the hardware-near driver layers of the Microcontroller Abstraction Layer (MCAL) via the ECU Abstraction Layer up to the standardized Internet transport and routing protocols in the Communication Services layer. The cluster addresses the increased bandwidth requirements of modern E/E architectures and seamlessly integrates standard vehicle protocols such as Diagnostic communication over IP (DoIP according to ISO 13400) and service-oriented communication (SOME/IP) into the AUTOSAR basic software by serving upper layers such as the Socket Adaptor (SoAd) SWS_TcpIp p. 123.

The three core modules of the cluster each assume clearly defined architectural responsibilities:

  • Ethernet Driver (Eth): As an MCAL module, Eth directly controls the Ethernet MAC controller. It manages the hardware-near transmit and receive buffer descriptors, controls MII/MDIO register interfaces for transceiver configuration ([SWS_Eth_00058]), activates physical filter rules ([SWS_Eth_00152]), and provides high-precision hardware timestamps for global time synchronization mechanisms ([SWS_Eth_00186], [SWS_Eth_00190]).
  • Ethernet Interface (EthIf): Forms the central abstraction layer and decouples upper layers from the physical hardware topology. EthIf abstracts multiple Ethernet controllers, switches, and transceivers (PHYs). It handles virtual LAN processing (VLAN tagging according to IEEE 802.1Q), frame type multiplexing, buffer assignments, and the aggregation of switch port groups and link states ([SWS_EthIf_00075], [SWS_EthIf_91102], AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 213).
  • TCP/IP Stack (TcpIp): Implements the Internet protocol family as a communication service. The module encompasses IPv4 and IPv6, dynamic address assignment via Auto-IP (RFC 3927) and DHCPv6 (RFC 3315) ([SWS_TCPIP_00057], [SWS_TCPIP_00166]), address resolution via ARP (RFC 826) ([SWS_TCPIP_00056]), connectionless transport via UDP, and connection-oriented, reliable byte-stream transport via TCP ([SWS_TCPIP_00050]). Furthermore, it enables transport encryption via TLS ([SWS_TCPIP_00300]).

Context diagram: Layered architecture and system context of the Ethernet Services cluster with module interactions. Sources: SWS_TcpIp p. 123, AUTOSAR_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 87, [SWS_EthIf_00075]

Interplay and Interaction Paths Between the Modules

The data transmission path (Transmission Path) is based on a two-stage buffer request and transmission procedure that supports a zero-copy design of the network card buffers. An upper protocol entity or the module TcpIp requests a contiguous memory buffer via EthIf_ProvideTxBuffer(), specifying priority and desired frame length ([SWS_Eth_00077], AUTOSAR_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 87). EthIf delegates this request to the corresponding driver by means of Eth_ProvideTxBuffer(), causing the driver to lock the hardware buffer and return a descriptor index (Eth_BufIdxType) as well as the buffer pointer ([SWS_Eth_00077]). After payload population, the calling layer initiates transmission via EthIf_Transmit() ([SWS_EthIf_00075]). When appropriately configured, EthIf inserts the VLAN tag (EtherType 0x8100) and calls Eth_Transmit(), whereupon the driver constructs the Ethernet header, sets the destination MAC address, and transfers the transmission request to the MAC controller ([SWS_Eth_00087], [SWS_EthIf_00250]).

Sequence diagram: Buffer allocation, data transmission, and asynchronous transmit confirmation in the Ethernet cluster. Sources: [SWS_Eth_00077], [SWS_Eth_00087], [SWS_EthIf_00075], [SWS_EthIf_00091]

The reception path (Reception Path) processes incoming Ethernet frames either event-driven from an interrupt or polling-based. After reading the buffer from the hardware queue using Eth_Receive() ([SWS_Eth_00095], [SWS_Eth_00162]), the driver signals the packet to the interface via EthIf_RxIndication() ([SWS_EthIf_00085]). EthIf verifies the validity of the controller and any VLAN tags, filters invalid datagrams ([SWS_EthIf_00309]), and forwards the frame to the assigned upper layer based on the EtherType. Received IP packets are handled by TcpIp, which evaluates the frame based on the referenced receive PDU (TcpIpCtrlRxPdu) and the metadata ([SWS_TcpIp_00411], [SWS_TcpIp_00412]). If the interface and destination IP fulfill the assignment conditions to the local address table ([SWS_TCPIP_00169]), the packet is unpacked and passed synchronously to the responsible socket owner (e.g., SoAd) via the interface <Up_RxIndication>() ([SWS_TCPIP_00220], [SWS_TCPIP_00223]).

Sequence diagram: Frame reception path and packet dispatching up to the socket layer. Sources: [SWS_Eth_00095], [SWS_EthIf_00085], [SWS_TCPIP_00169], [SWS_TCPIP_00223]

In the area of address resolution and packet filtering, TcpIp and Eth interact closely via EthIf. If TcpIp discovers new address relationships via incoming packets or ARP replies, it updates the ARP cache ([SWS_TCPIP_00056], [SWS_TcpIp_00092]) and reports changes via Up_PhysAddrTableChg() ([SWS_TCPIP_00142]). In the absence of a MAC address, TcpIp_GetRemotePhysAddr() initiates an address resolution ([SWS_TCPIP_00137]). To limit network broadcasts and multicast traffic, EthIf configures hardware-supported hash filters or tables in the MAC controller via Eth_UpdatePhysAddrFilter() in order to selectively forward or drop multicast frames on Layer 2 ([SWS_Eth_00152], [SWS_Eth_00245]).

Synchronization, reentrancy and task contexts

The module cluster supports two operating modes for temporal decoupling: polling mode and interrupt mode. In polling mode, the cyclic function EthIf_MainFunctionTx() at task level handles querying completed transmission processes by calling Eth_TxConfirmation() for all configured drivers ([SWS_EthIf_00115], AUTOSAR_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 87). Similarly, receive queues are drained via periodic calls of Eth_Receive() in the task context ([SWS_Eth_00095]). In interrupt mode, transmit and receive ISRs (Eth_TxIrqHdlr_<CtrlIdx>(), Eth_RxIrqHdlr_<CtrlIdx>()) report events directly from the interrupt context to EthIf_TxConfirmation() and EthIf_RxIndication() ([SWS_EthIf_00091], AUTOSAR_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 88, SWS_EthernetInterface p. 173). The cyclic state monitoring of transceiver and switch connections takes place decoupled in EthIf_MainFunctionState() (AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_EthernetInterface p. 213).

The reentrancy requirements are precisely tailored to multi-core and multitasking systems. Eth_ProvideTxBuffer() is designed to be fully reentrant ([SWS_Eth_00077]). The transmit APIs Eth_Transmit() and EthIf_Transmit() are reentrant for different controller and buffer indices ([SWS_Eth_00087], [SWS_EthIf_00075]). In contrast, control functions such as Eth_SetPhysAddr() or Eth_UpdatePhysAddrFilter() are non-reentrant for the same controller, but may be executed concurrently for different controllers ([SWS_Eth_00151], [SWS_Eth_00152]). Status acquisitions and hardware timestamp queries (e.g., Eth_GetCurrentTime() and EthIf_GetCurrentTime(), respectively) are explicitly specified for invocation within exclusive areas in order to ensure jitter-free timestamp consistency for protocols such as gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS) (SWS_EthernetDriver p. 82, SWS_EthernetInterface p. 140).

Typical lifecycles and operating modes

The lifecycle of the cluster requires a strict initialization sequence, which is typically controlled by the ECU State Manager (EcuM): first, the hardware-near driver is initialized by means of Eth_Init(), followed by EthIf_Init(), and finally the protocol stack TcpIp_Init(). In regular operation, all interfaces verify whether initialization completed successfully and otherwise refuse execution while signaling development errors ([SWS_Eth_00027], [SWS_Eth_00051], [SWS_EthIf_00024]).

Layer 2 mode management is controlled via EthIf_SetControllerMode(), whereby the mode of the addressed controller is transitioned between ETH_MODE_DOWN, ETH_MODE_ACTIVE, and ETH_MODE_ACTIVE_WITH_WAKEUP_REQUEST ([SWS_EthIf_00034], [SWS_Eth_91008]). The driver performs the mode transition and confirms it asynchronously via the callback EthIf_CtrlModeIndication(), which forwards the state change to the Ethernet State Manager (EthSM) ([SWS_EthIf_00231], [SWS_EthIf_00252]). For networked switches, EthIf additionally controls switch port groups by means of EthIf_SwitchPortGroupRequestMode() or starts all ports via EthIf_StartAllPorts() ([SWS_EthIf_91102], [SWS_EthIf_91103]). In the TcpIp stack, the network's communication state is controlled separately via TcpIp_RequestComMode(): TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE activates IP address assignment, TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD pauses transmission activities, and TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE closes all active sockets ([SWS_TCPIP_00070], [SWS_TCPIP_00071], [SWS_TCPIP_00072], [SWS_TCPIP_00074]).

In the areas of shutdown, sleep, and wakeup, the cluster supports standardized wakeup sequences according to OPEN Alliance TC10 (SWS_ECUStateManager p. 192). If the Ethernet hardware (PHY or switch port) detects a wakeup signal in sleep state, an interrupt signals the event. The integration code or EcuM then triggers EthIf_CheckWakeup(), which instructs the affected transceiver drivers to perform asynchronous verification ([SWS_EthIf_00244], [SWS_EthIf_00245]). Detailed wakeup reasons can be read out via EthIf_GetSwitchPortWakeupReason() ([SWS_EthIf_91005]). During shutdown, TcpIp_ResetIpAssignment() allows persisted IP assignments in the NvM to be reset specifically ([SWS_TCPIP_00215], [SWS_TCPIP_00216]).

Error Handling, DET Tracing, and Degradation

The modules of the cluster implement a multi-stage error monitoring and diagnostic concept. During development and system integration, the Default Error Tracer (DET) intercepts programming and configuration errors. These include calls prior to successful module initialization (ETH_E_UNINIT, ETHIF_E_UNINIT) ([SWS_Eth_00228], [SWS_EthIf_00036]), invalid controller or transceiver indices (ETH_E_INV_CTRL_IDX, ETHIF_E_INV_TRCV_IDX) ([SWS_Eth_00229], [SWS_EthIf_00326]), and invalid pointer parameters ([SWS_Eth_00230], [SWS_Eth_00250]). In case of hardware-related communication disturbances on the MII bus, Eth_WriteMii() reports the runtime error ETH_E_COMMUNICATION ([SWS_Eth_00058], [SWS_Eth_00286]).

For operational diagnostics and diagnostic event management (DEM), Eth and EthIf provide standardized counter structures in accordance with IETF RFC standards. Via Eth_GetCounterValues() and Eth_GetRxStats(), drop events caused by buffer overruns, CRC errors, oversized and undersized packets (jabbers, undersize), and alignment errors according to RFC 1757, RFC 1643, and RFC 2819 are captured ([SWS_Eth_00226], [SWS_Eth_00233], [SWS_Eth_91007], [SWS_Eth_91002]). Transmit counters and error statistics are provided by means of Eth_GetTxStats() and Eth_GetTxErrorCounterValues() ([SWS_Eth_91005], [SWS_Eth_91006], [SWS_Eth_91003]). EthIf transparently forwards these counter queries for external switch hardware via EthIf_SwitchPortGetCounterValues() and EthIf_SwitchPortGetTxErrorCounterValues() ([SWS_EthIf_91115], [SWS_EthIf_91118]).

Degradation mechanisms and link quality monitoring ensure functional robustness: EthIf_GetTrcvSignalQuality() provides current, minimum, and maximum link qualities of the physical transceivers ([SWS_EthIf_91056], [SWS_EthIf_91057]), allowing degraded transmission links to be diagnosed before link drop occurs. EthIf_GetAndResetMeasurementData() enables reading out and resetting detailed measurement data on dropped datagrams, for instance in case of configuration deficiencies regarding VLAN IDs or controller assignments ([SWS_EthIf_91011], [SWS_EthIf_00309]). In the event of link losses, EthIf_Transmit() stops forwarding to the driver ([SWS_EthIf_00076]), while TcpIp terminates sockets and clears transmit queues in offline states ([SWS_TCPIP_00072]).

This guide is based exclusively on the specifications of AUTOSAR Classic Platform Release R20-11.
